q: Is the printed bare eq (2.5) genuinely stable at the published MCF7 fit, or was the Table-2 cap (Y_max=300, Z_max=1000) applied silently in Fig 4b integration? Our local check finds k3*k5/(k4*k6) = 1.000374 > 1 (post-repair fixed point is a saddle, det J = -145), so bare integration to 24 h yields <Y>=3622 and <Z>=11313 --- both >> the Table-2 caps.
basis: REPORT.md §3 (C-STABILITY-MCF7) and §7 blocker #7. Local stability analysis of the (Y,Z) subsystem at (X=0, Y=Y*, Z=Z*) with MCF7 Table-1 constants; direct integration in scripts/smoke_model.py to 24 h with bare eq (2.5); ratio k3*k5/(k4*k6) computed exactly. MDA-MB-468 sits at 0.987, marginally stable, showing the fitted regime is generically near-bifurcation. Paper does not print any cap in eq (2.5) as displayed, nor discuss stability of the post-repair fixed point.
next_steps: (a) Contact the corresponding author (S.J. Chapman, Oxford) to ask (i) which integration horizon was used for Fig 4b and (ii) whether Y_max/Z_max caps were applied silently. (b) If caps were applied, re-fit Table 1 for MCF7 under the constraint k3*k5/(k4*k6) < 1 and check whether the fit quality on Fig 4b degrades. (c) If no cap was applied, then Fig 4b as printed cannot correspond to eq (2.5) as printed at those parameters and one of the two must be corrected.

q: Does the 6-parameter Nelder-Mead fit (eq 3.3) genuinely have predictive power on held-out DSB kinetics, or is it a descriptive over-fit to ~14 time points? The paper reports no cross-validation, no held-out data, and no comparison against a simpler two-timescale exponential-decay baseline.
basis: Paper §3 lays out eq (3.3) cost against Fig 4 time series; Fig 4 shows ~7 nominal time points per cell line × 2 observables (foci and comet OTM) = 14 fitted numbers against 6 free rate constants. Paper's discussion (§5) treats the fit as validation of the model rather than as a descriptive fit to be tested. No bootstrap, no leave-one-out, no external cohort.
next_steps: (a) WebPlotDigitizer extraction of Fig 4a/b for both cell lines (~2 h) to recover the (t, foci, OTM) points; (b) leave-one-out cross-validation: refit on 6 of 7 time points, predict the seventh; (c) side-by-side comparison against a 2-parameter bi-exponential decay ansatz f(t) = A*exp(-t/T1) + B*exp(-t/T2); (d) if the 6-parameter model does not substantially out-predict the 2-parameter baseline on held-out points, the mechanistic interpretation of k1..k6 is weakened.

q: How does this framework compare quantitatively against competing DSB-repair theoretical frameworks (e.g. two-lesion kinetic model of Cucinotta-Nikjoo, radiator/repair rate-equation models of Herr-Friedland, or MEDRAS-family models used in TOPAS-nBio)? The paper does not perform head-to-head model comparison; it cites but does not benchmark against these.
basis: Paper's Introduction §1 cites prior mathematical models of DSB repair but does not run any of them on the same MCF7/MDA-MB-468 datasets. Its own Table 1 fit is compared only to itself. No AIC/BIC across frameworks; no Bayes-factor comparison.
next_steps: (a) Choose 1-2 competing frameworks with clean formulations (bi-exponential; Cucinotta two-lesion; a repair-priority-queue variant); (b) fit each on the same Fig 4 extracted data with matched loss; (c) compute AIC/BIC and cross-validated NLL; (d) report which framework's inductive bias (single-Markov-site + closures vs two-lesion vs empirical bi-exponential) is best supported by the ~14-point data. This is the single highest-value open question because it tests whether the theoretical apparatus buys anything beyond curve-fitting.

q: What is the quantitative mapping between the SSA (eq 2.1) limit and the ODE (eq 2.5 / 2.8) limits? The paper asserts eq 2.5/2.8 are moment closures of 2.1 but does not report an SSA-vs-ODE convergence study as a function of system size or trajectory count.
basis: Paper §3 states the closures track SSA means "well"; Fig 3 shows one overlay per closure per cell line without a quantitative RMS or convergence-in-N table. Our local closure_validation gives RMS Z ~56 for MDA-MB-468 (SSA peak Z~445; ~13%) and ~104 for MCF7 (SSA peak Z~800; ~13%), noticeably looser than the paper's overlays suggest visually. Whether this is tau-leap bias, true closure bias, or a difference in n-trajectory averaging is not distinguished by the paper.
next_steps: (a) Run exact Gillespie for n = 10, 100, 1000, 10000 trajectories, both cell lines, to isolate n-averaging noise from closure bias; (b) compare exact-SSA mean at each t vs bare eq (2.5) and eq (2.8) with matched initial conditions; (c) report RMS as function of n and of t-horizon; (d) if closure bias is >5% on the dynamic range of <Z>, the closures are describing but not quantitatively tracking the underlying stochastic dynamics --- worth an erratum-level correction.

q: Does the framework make testable predictions at parameter extremes not covered by the fitting regime --- FLASH dose rate (>40 Gy/s), ultra-low-dose (<0.01 Gy), or extreme-high-LET (Auger clusters, alpha, HZE ions)? The Auger extension is the only high-LET case actually implemented, and it uses a single R sweep in a small range (R=0..8).
basis: Paper fits at 4 Gy X-ray dose (typical of MCF7/MDA-MB-468 experimental range in refs [12,17]). Eq (4.3) Auger extension is exercised at nominal specific-activity values but paper does not test at the physically extreme cases (FLASH would violate the k1-drives-X assumption if DSB induction happens on a timescale faster than pATM binding; ultra-low-dose would push single-DSB assumption harder; high-LET would violate the Poisson-DSB-induction assumption if damage clusters cluster).
next_steps: (a) Push the SSA to a dose-rate regime with instantaneous vs finite-duration DSB induction (delta-function vs boxcar in eq 2.1); (b) test single-DSB-limit vs multi-DSB extension where DSBs may compete for a finite pATM pool (paper's k4 is assumed density-independent); (c) run the Auger case at cluster-DSB parameter regimes where the Poisson-induction assumption breaks; (d) any of these excursions that shows a qualitative change in the AUC persistence measure defines a genuine testable prediction of the framework worth taking to experiment. This is the strongest scientific-value open question.
